chapters.summary: Proverbs opens by declaring the value of wisdom, urging the reader to fear the LORD, turn away from the enticement of the wicked, and heed wisdom's call.
keyPoints: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Listen to your parents' instruction and do not follow the wicked, so that you are not caught in the snare of sin.
Wisdom cries out in the marketplace, promising peace to those who find her and disaster to those who refuse her.
chapters.application: Seek wisdom every day with a humble heart, listen to God's word, refuse the enticement of sin, and rely on God in your decisions so that you may enjoy peace and blessing.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches us to seek wisdom and understanding wholeheartedly, for the LORD gives wisdom and grants insight into righteousness, justice, and integrity, keeping those who walk in the way of righteousness.
keyPoints: Incline your ear to wisdom and apply your heart to understanding, searching for it as for silver, and you will come to know the fear of the LORD.
The LORD gives wisdom; knowledge and understanding come from his mouth, and he stores up sound wisdom for the upright.
Wisdom will guard you and deliver you from evil ways and from the adulterous woman, and will lead you to walk in the way of good men.
chapters.application: Long for God's word every day as one who searches for treasure; ask him in your decisions, and he will guide you into the right path and guard you from temptation.

chapters.summary: This chapter urges us to trust the LORD with our whole heart and treasure wisdom above all things, emphasizing God's care and guidance for those who obey him.
keyPoints: Do not forget God's law; keep truth and devotion in your heart, and you will find long life and peace.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart and do not lean on your own understanding, but acknowledge him in all your ways.
Treasure wisdom above all things, for gaining wisdom is better than gaining silver or gold, and it brings life and honor.
chapters.application: Seek God's will first each day and entrust everything to him rather than following your own judgment; long for wisdom, and with the fear of God as your foundation you will surely be guided and blessed.

chapters.summary: This chapter stresses the importance of wisdom, urging children to receive instruction and hold fast to wisdom, for wisdom is the fountain of life and light.
keyPoints: Wisdom is the source of life; hold fast to it and do not let it go.
Pay attention to the words of wisdom, for they are life and healing.
Guard your heart above all else, for from it flow the springs of life.
chapters.application: Read the word and pray every day, asking God to give you wisdom and to guard your thoughts, so that you may walk in the light.

chapters.summary: In this chapter a father urges his son to heed the words of wisdom, warns him against the adulterous woman, and stresses faithfulness and joy within marriage.
keyPoints: Pay attention to the words of wisdom and keep them in your heart, that you may gain knowledge and discretion.
The lips of the adulterous woman drip honey, but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood and as sharp as a two-edged sword.
Rejoice in the wife of your youth, and let her love satisfy you always.
chapters.application: Ask God for wisdom every day to guard your heart against temptation; treasure your spouse in marriage and build your household on faithfulness and love.

chapters.summary: This chapter warns against putting up security for others, against laziness, and against wrongdoing, lists seven things the LORD hates, and urges us to keep our parents' commands and turn away from the adulterous woman.
keyPoints: Do not put up security for your neighbor, lest you be snared; free yourself at once, like a bird escaping the hand of the fowler.
The sluggard should learn from the ant, preparing diligently, lest poverty come upon him like a robber.
Seven things the LORD hates are listed, warning us not to do evil and to keep our parents' commands.
chapters.application: Today let us watch our words and not rashly pledge ourselves for others; let us work diligently and turn from laziness, and examine ourselves so that we turn away from what God hates and live holy lives.

chapters.summary: In this chapter a father urges his son to hold fast to wisdom and beware the enticement of the adulterous woman, describing how a young man is caught in the snare of lust.
keyPoints: Keep the commands of wisdom as the apple of your eye, and stay far from the words of the adulterous woman.
A senseless young man is drawn along after her, like an ox going to the slaughter, until it costs him his life.
Her path leads down to Sheol and the chambers of death; only those who heed wisdom will live.
chapters.application: In daily life, stay alert to temptation, hold to God's word as your standard, guard your heart, turn away from trials, and choose the path of life.

chapters.summary: Wisdom cries aloud in the streets, urging people to receive instruction, and declares her worth to be greater than silver and gold.
keyPoints: Wisdom raises her voice where people gather, calling the world to turn back.
Wisdom is better than silver and rubies, and she grants wealth and honor.
Wisdom existed from the very beginning, took part in creation, and delights in mankind.
chapters.application: Seek wisdom every day above the pursuit of material wealth; heed wisdom's guidance in your decisions, and you will find life and blessing.

chapters.summary: This chapter contrasts the invitations of wisdom and folly, calling us to fear the LORD and gain wisdom, and to turn away from folly and pride.
keyPoints: Wisdom builds her house and prepares a feast, inviting people to come and gain understanding.
Wisdom teaches that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and to know the Holy One is understanding.
The foolish woman calls loudly and lures people in, but her guests are in the depths of Sheol, warning us to turn away from folly.
chapters.application: Choose every day to fear God and receive wisdom, turning away from the enticement of folly, so that your life grows on the right path.

chapters.summary: By contrasting the words and deeds of the righteous and the wicked, this chapter shows that wisdom and righteousness bring blessing, while folly and wickedness bring calamity.
keyPoints: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
Lazy hands bring poverty, but diligent hands bring wealth.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
chapters.application: Examine your words and actions every day; choose wisdom and righteousness, treat others with diligence and honesty, and you will surely please God and enjoy peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes the importance of integrity and honesty, showing that the righteous are blessed and the wicked come to ruin, and urging us to trust God and be generous to others.
keyPoints: The LORD detests dishonest scales but delights in a just weight; honesty is the foundation of a life well lived.
Pride brings disgrace, but humility brings wisdom; humility is the path to grace.
The mouth of the righteous bears good fruit, but the tongue of the wicked brings calamity; our words reveal our hearts.
chapters.application: In all you do today, let honesty and integrity be your foundation; keep a humble heart, guard your words, and give generously, so that you may please God and enjoy peace and blessing.

chapters.summary: By contrasting the words, deeds, and hearts of the righteous and the wicked, this chapter teaches that the wise receive discipline and the upright please God.
keyPoints: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Anxiety weighs down the heart, but a kind word brings joy.
chapters.application: Pay attention to your words each day; speak more words that build others up, and humbly receive correction, so that your life overflows with wisdom and peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter contrasts the outcomes of wisdom and folly, righteousness and wickedness, stressing the importance of guarding our words, working diligently, and receiving discipline.
keyPoints: A wise son heeds his father's instruction, but a scoffer does not listen to rebuke, showing the difference between humility and pride.
Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life, but whoever opens wide his lips comes to ruin; our words are a matter of life and death.
The diligent who plan carefully come to abundance, but the hasty come only to poverty; diligence brings wealth.
chapters.application: Examine your words and actions every day; choose to listen to wise correction and face life with diligence and honesty, and God will surely bless you.

chapters.summary: This chapter contrasts the different paths and outcomes of wisdom and folly, of fearing God and despising him.
keyPoints: The wise woman builds her house, but the foolish tears it down with her own hands.
The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
chapters.application: Examine your words and actions every day; choose the wisdom that fears God, and face life with a peaceful heart, so that your family and relationships are built up.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes the importance of gentle speech, wise instruction, and the fear of the LORD, showing the different outcomes for the righteous and the wicked.
keyPoints: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but harsh words stir up anger.
The wise receive discipline, but fools despise instruction; humility and the fear of the LORD are the way of life.
The fear of the LORD brings wealth, honor, and life; turning away from evil is the beginning of wisdom.
chapters.application: Before you speak today, ask the Lord for a gentle heart to answer others with wisdom; humbly receive correction, and walking in the fear of God you will surely find life and peace.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches that although man plans, God is sovereign over all, urging us to humbly rely on him and to act with steadfast love and truth.
keyPoints: The heart of man plans his way, but it is the LORD who directs his steps.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of God's throne, and a king should rule with righteousness.
themes: Humility and the Fear of God
chapters.application: Entrust your plans to God each day, keep a humble heart, treat others with honesty and love, and trust that God will direct your steps.

chapters.summary: This chapter stresses harmony in the family, wise speech, and a compassionate heart, pointing out the harm of folly and pride, and teaching how to treat others with love and wisdom.
keyPoints: A peaceful home is better than a house full of feasting, while quarreling and pride bring strife.
The wise are careful in speech, but fools bring ruin on themselves through much talk and mockery.
To show mercy to the poor is to honor God, but to mock the needy invites judgment.
chapters.application: Today, value harmony above all, guard your tongue, and cultivate a compassionate heart toward others, so that you may glorify God in this way.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes the power of words and the importance of wisdom, urging us to be careful in speech and to seek true wisdom.
keyPoints: Whoever isolates himself does himself harm; seek fellowship with others instead.
Words carry the power of life and death, blessing and calamity, so speak with care.
Wealth and honor come from humility and the fear of the LORD.
themes: Humility and the Fear of God
chapters.application: In daily life, pay attention to your words and speak more to build others up; at the same time keep a humble heart, fear God, and pursue wisdom, so that pride and folly do not bring you harm.

chapters.summary: This chapter stresses the importance of honesty, the fear of God, and wisdom, points out the relative worth of poverty and wealth, and urges us to pursue true virtue.
keyPoints: Honesty and integrity are more precious than wealth, and a fool brings calamity on himself through his own mouth.
The fear of the LORD is the way of life, keeping a person from evil.
Laziness brings poverty, but diligence brings wealth, and to show mercy to the poor is an honor.
chapters.application: In daily life, treat others honestly, fear God, work diligently, and be willing to help those in need.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes wisdom, righteousness, and self-control, urging us to rely on God and turn away from folly and falsehood.
keyPoints: Wine leads to recklessness and drunkenness easily brings strife; sobriety and self-control are essential.
The heart of man devises many plans, but it is the LORD who establishes his steps, so we should humbly rely on God.
Honesty and righteousness are the foundation of a nation, while falsehood and bribery bring ruin.
chapters.application: Guard your speech each day and turn away from the temptation of drunkenness; do not act on your own judgment but seek God first, and deal with others honestly and fairly, and you will surely please God.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes that the LORD governs the hearts of men, urging us to pursue righteousness and wisdom and to turn far from pride and laziness.
keyPoints: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, like a channel of water that he turns wherever he wills.
To do righteousness and justice is more pleasing to the LORD than sacrifice.
Whoever pursues righteousness and love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
chapters.application: Seek God's guidance first in every decision, act with honesty and love, avoid pride and laziness, and trust that God is sovereign over all things.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes the importance of humility, the fear of the LORD, and wisdom, and teaches principles for raising children and dealing with others.
keyPoints: A good name is better than great riches, and favor is better than silver or gold, reminding us to value reputation and character.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not depart from it, stressing the importance of early instruction.
The reward for the fear of the LORD and a humble heart is riches, honor, and life.
themes: Humility and the Fear of God
chapters.application: Let us pursue a good name in our daily lives, act with a humble and reverent heart, and patiently teach the next generation to walk in the right way.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches us how to face wealth, feasting, and power with wisdom, emphasizing humility, contentment, and the fear of the LORD.
keyPoints: Do not crave the delicacies of a ruler, for such food is deceptive.
Do not wear yourself out to get rich, for wealth is fleeting.
Pay attention to instruction so that your heart is filled with wisdom, and you find hope.
themes: Self-Control and the Fear of God
chapters.application: When facing temptation and trial, ask God for wisdom, receive your daily bread with a contented heart, rely fully on him, and do not turn from the right path for the sake of fleeting gain.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches the wise to draw their strength from God, warns against the way of the wicked, and encourages doing good and working diligently.
keyPoints: Do not envy the wicked, for their end is destruction.
The wise are mighty in strength, and knowledge multiplies power.
Do not gloat over the misfortune of others, but stand up for those who are wronged.
chapters.application: In daily life, act with wisdom, do not envy the wicked, rely on God for strength, and be willing to help those in need.

chapters.summary: This chapter gathers proverbs of Solomon copied out by the men of Hezekiah, teaching kings and people alike how to conduct themselves with humility, patience, and wisdom.
keyPoints: It is God's glory to conceal a matter, but the heart of a king is unsearchable and must be searched out.
Remove the dross from silver, and a throne is established through righteousness.
We are urged to wait humbly for promotion, which is better than exalting ourselves only to be brought low.
chapters.application: In your dealings with others today, keep a humble heart, do not rush to defend yourself or seek status, resolve conflict with gentle words, and wait for God to exalt you at the right time.

chapters.summary: Through a series of comparisons and contrasts, this chapter teaches the difference between wisdom and folly, and the consequences of our words and deeds.
keyPoints: Honor is not fitting for a fool, like snow in summer, out of place.
Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him yourself; yet answer him, lest he think himself wise.
The sluggard turns on his bed like a door on its hinges, never making progress and wasting his time.
chapters.application: Ask the Lord to give us wisdom to guard our speech, turn away from laziness, and work diligently every day, so that we glorify God.

chapters.summary: Through several sets of contrasts, this chapter teaches a life of wisdom, emphasizing the value of humility, honesty, diligence, and true friendship.
keyPoints: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful and excessive.
Diligent labor brings full provision, while chasing empty pursuits brings poverty.
chapters.application: Today, rely on God with a humble heart, treasure honest friends who offer correction, do your work diligently, and entrust the future into his hand.

chapters.summary: This chapter emphasizes the importance of righteousness and wisdom, showing that although the wicked may prosper for a time they will surely come to ruin, while the righteous will be kept safe.
keyPoints: The wicked flee though no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food, but whoever seeks the LORD will lack nothing good.
Whoever confesses and forsakes their sins finds mercy, but whoever conceals their sins will not prosper.
chapters.application: Examine your conduct every day, turn away from wickedness, rely on God to do what is right, find mercy through repentance, and live an upright life.

chapters.summary: This chapter stresses the importance of righteousness and wisdom, showing that both kings and people should make the fear of the LORD their foundation, turning away from wrongdoing to enjoy peace.
keyPoints: One who is often rebuked yet stiffens his neck will suddenly be broken beyond healing.
When the righteous increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan; righteousness exalts a nation.
A fool gives full vent to his anger, but the wise quietly holds it back; humility and the fear of the LORD are the source of wisdom.
chapters.application: In daily life, receive correction with a humble and teachable heart rather than hardening it; act righteously, speak gently, and fear God, so that your family and community may enjoy peace.

chapters.summary: The words of Agur, who humbly confesses his own limitations, asks God for his daily bread, and lists wonders that display God's wisdom in creation, warning against pride and folly.
keyPoints: Agur confesses his own limitation, acknowledging that he cannot fathom the things of God.
He asks God for his daily bread, that he be given neither poverty nor riches.
He lists four wonders that display the wisdom of God's creation.
chapters.application: Humbly rely on God rather than your own understanding; ask him to give you your daily bread so that you are neither poor nor rich, and fix your trust wholly in him.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the words of King Lemuel, praising the character and worth of the excellent wife, and stressing that the fear of the LORD is the foundation of wisdom.
keyPoints: His mother warns the king to turn away from wine and women, to rule with justice, and to speak up for those who cannot defend themselves.
The excellent wife is worth far more than jewels; she works diligently, provides for her household, and gives to the poor.
She fears the LORD, clothes herself with strength and dignity, and does her husband good all the days of her life.
themes: The Virtue of a Godly Wife
chapters.application: Let us today treasure the godly women in our families, make the fear of God the foundation of our lives, and faithfully fulfill our own callings so that we become a blessing to others.
